# State of Agent Skills

State of Agent Skills is a method for writing an honest biweekly report about what really moved in an agent-skill catalogue. It starts from verified snapshots, never from a summary or a previous edition. For each edition, it fixes the covered period and the cutoff night, then recounts from the source: file-change events, affected listings, distinct sellers and hosts, changes per night, how often listings changed, the median gap between two changes of the same file, final outcomes in the current categories, and series coverage.

The report states what the series covers and what it does not cover. A file change is not proof of an improvement, and a disappearance is not proof of a sale. The draft is written in full in English and in French, each language on its own page, and short announcement posts only link to the page. Nothing is published until a separate go is given for that exact edition, and a go for one edition never covers the next one.

The reference method comes from edition 2, published on 2026-10-24, covering data from 3 to 23 October 2026, with a clean comparable series of 12 nights from 12 to 23 October: 486 file-change events and 296 affected listings, recounted in the source. Edition 1, on 2026-10-10, stayed a draft and was never published. The cadence is biweekly, not weekly and not monthly, with a reminder two weeks after each published edition.
